newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Well-supported OLO mkt should hold ground -dealers.
newsitem.headline: Well-supported OLO mkt should hold ground -dealers.

text.p: Belgian cash bonds and futures slipped in a widespread bout of weakness on markets worried by stronger than expected German data and reports of U.S. Federal Reserve officials being concerned about inflation.

But dealers said the Belgian market had held up relatively well, outperforming German Bunds on the way down and causing the yield spread below 10-year OLOs and Bunds to narrow slightly to 15 basis points from 16 late on Tuesday.
They said the market in general was still well-supported with few players willing to cash in capital gains for fear of large tax bills. A lack of spare cash limited buying potential.
"The Belgian market is stuck," said a trader.

As a crisis over child sex allegations against a deputy prime minister approached the end of its third week day, dealers said they had managed to convince mainly foreign investors that the government was in no risk of collapsing.
"End-investors do not seem too worried about the recent scandal, but they are not buying either, hence a risk of spread widening," said a trader.
"Even if Elio Di Rupo (the minister) were to resign, the government will stay," another said. Di Rupo has strongly denied the allegations of paedophile sex, made in the media.
Members of a parliament commission looking into the allegations have said the case against him was thin.

The commission, which began its meeting at 0900 GMT, suspended its deliberations at 1530 GMT and was due to reconvene at 1800 GMT. There was no immediate indication of the progress made so far or when it might conclude.
If the commission recommends Di Rupo be sent before Belgium's highest court, his career will be over.
The U.S. inflation worries and stronger than expected German M3 money and Ifo business climate data dampened German rate cut hopes, hitting four- to eight-year Belgian paper hardest.
"Retail investor and bank demand for OLOs seems to have dried up," said a trader. But the shorter end was supported by ample liquidity conditions and a steady franc, he noted.

Pressure on the 2006 benchmark OLO was limited, with its yield nudging up to 5.99 percent, three basis points above Tuesday's close. December bond futures lost 0.18 at 120.21, just over half the loss of comparable German futures.
